iter11 cycle4: READY per brief (bool FUN_005aeed0(undefined4* p) = WaitForSingleObject((HANDLE)*p, 0) != 0x102; SAFE non-blocking poll; caller 0x005ab620 C2; arg_type ptr_arg_int_get). AUTHORING HELD — DEGENERACY RISK, not a safety risk: ptr_arg_int_get seeds the buffer with arbitrary ints, so every seed is an invalid HANDLE, WaitForSingleObject returns WAIT_FAILED (0xffffffff) != 0x102, and EVERY test returns 1. That is a bit-identical GREEN that proves nothing (INCONCLUSIVE-DEGENERATE, cf. 0x004c1a00). To make it evidential the seed must carry a REAL handle plus at least one signalled/unsignalled pair so both branches of the 0x102 compare are exercised. Needs a scenario-attach seed, not a synthetic one.

iter11 cycle4: READY per brief (RwStringGetSizeAligned, uint fn(char*), strlen then (len+4)&0xfffffffc; SAFE, no global writes; caller 0x004cf4a0 C2; arg_type ptr_arg_int_get; 34B). AUTHORING HELD — SEED TERMINATION HAZARD: ptr_arg_int_get allocates a buffer of seeded ints with no guaranteed NUL, so strlen can run past the allocation. This project already hit exactly this (FontText 0x427840 strlen(NULL) crash, memory feedback_diff_reimpl_asm_vs_original). Fix is cheap and this row is otherwise the BEST candidate seen so far — pure function, non-degenerate by construction (distinct strings give distinct aligned sizes). Needs either a NUL-terminated string seed variant of ptr_arg_int_get or a small new str_arg_int_get handler.
